notes: §1985:VI.6.13.4 GR1: the statement 'operates as if each selection subject and selection object were evaluated and assigned a numeric or nonnumeric value, a range of numeric or nonnumeric values, or a truth value', by items a to h. EvaluateBinder.Bind evaluates every subject once at the start (one SubjectSlot each, BindSubjectValue) and BindWhenItem assigns each object its value by form: ANY a constant true (f), TRUE/FALSE and condition-1/-2 a truth value (d, e), an identifier, literal or arithmetic expression an equality operand compared by the relation rules (a to c; ZERO takes the subject's class through the figurative-constant comparison, b), THROUGH an inclusive pair (g, BindRangeObject) and NOT a negation of the whole term (h, BindSelectionObject). Probed at --std 85 beyond the witness (alphanumeric and numeric ZERO, identifier and literal ranges under PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE, NOT range, expression subject and object, condition subject, literal subjects, TRUE/FALSE pairs): all as the rule assigns. PARTIAL: there is no edition arm, and the objects are evaluated pair by pair inside the emitted if / else-if chain (EvaluateEmitter.Emit), the 2023 order (§2023:14.9.13.4 GR4 'no more pairs in that WHEN phrase are evaluated'); the 1985 model evaluates EACH selection object, which is observable when a selection object the chain never reaches references FUNCTION RANDOM (X3.23a-1989, a function's value 'is derived automatically at the time of reference'): the object's reference is skipped at 85 and the pseudo-random sequence a later statement reads differs. Every object without a function reference (all of the 1985 base language) is unaffected. No kb/Work note owns it (grepped 'as if each selection subject', VI.6.13, RANDOM with EVALUATE; PB5069-PB5130): the orchestrator files one. Lead met on the way, not this rule's: `EVALUATE N WHEN > 5` (a 2002 partial-expression object, absent from the §1985:VI.6.13.2 format) compiles and runs at --std 85 with no COBOL0900 (probe e3.cob); it belongs to 1985-FMT-VI.6.13.2; kb/Work PB398 (landed) left the object ungated on purpose while the repository held no 1985 text ('the one judgment an owner may want to overturn'), and no open note carries it.

next.reason: 1985 'operates as if each selection subject and selection object were evaluated and assigned' a value. §2023:14.9.13.4 GR3 evaluates the subjects at the start but §2023:14.9.13.4 GR4 evaluates objects pair by pair: 'no more pairs in that WHEN phrase are evaluated' and later WHENs are not analyzed. A 1985 (X3.23a-1989) program whose skipped object references FUNCTION RANDOM (§1989:A.2.35.3 AR4 'return the next number in the current sequence') gets a different later value. Value, class and range assignment are kept (§2023:14.9.13.4 GR1, GR2, GR4).
